description:
About the Position

The Department of Meteorology at Stockholm University invites applications for a PhD student position in atmospheric sciences and oceanography, focused on aerosol-cloud-climate interactions. The project studies how atmospheric particles influence cloud properties and, through them, the climate system - one of the largest sources of uncertainty in climate projection. The doctoral candidate will work with observations, cloud-resolving or global models, and possibly field-campaign data, within a salaried four-year employment under the Swedish collective agreement.

Stockholm's Department of Meteorology (MISU) is a leading Nordic centre for atmospheric and climate research, with a long tradition in cloud physics and air-sea interaction. Doctoral researchers join an international group, participate in Nordic and European research collaborations, and receive training in atmospheric physics, data analysis and scientific computing. The department's location within the Swedish climate research community provides access to national supercomputing resources and observational infrastructure.

Candidate Profile

Applicants hold a master's degree in meteorology, physics, environmental science or a related quantitative discipline, with strong mathematics and programming skills. Interest in cloud processes and climate modelling is essential; prior experience with radar or satellite data, model experiments or field campaigns is an advantage. Applications are submitted through the Varbi recruitment system with CV, transcripts, references and a statement of interest.

Highlights

  • PhD on aerosol-cloud-climate interactions at Stockholm MISU
  • Leading Nordic atmospheric and climate research department
  • Observations and cloud-resolving or global modelling
  • Salaried four-year employment per Swedish collective agreement
  • National supercomputing and observational infrastructure
  • Application via the Varbi recruitment system

About Stockholm University

Stockholm University is a public research university in the Swedish capital with roughly 30,000 students and a strong research profile in the natural sciences, psychology, humanities, law and social sciences. Many of its departments collaborate with national research institutes located on the same campus areas, including the neighbouring Science for Life Laboratory environment. Doctoral students in Sweden are employed on paid contracts with collective-agreement salaries and full social benefits. PhD and postdoctoral vacancies are recruited through the national Varbi system used by Swedish universities.
